articles.title: QatarEnergy acquires 25% stake in Sintana-exposed PEL 82 offshore Namibia
articles.summary:
Sintana Energy CEO Robert Bose joined Steve Darling from Proactive to discuss QatarEnergy's agreement to acquire a 25% participating interest in Petroleum Exploration Licence 82 (PEL 82), offshore Namibia, from an affiliate of Chevron Corporation.

The transaction brings another major international energy company into the licence, while leaving the interests held by Sintana Energy and its subsidiary, Custos Energy, unchanged.

Bose told Proactive that Chevron will retain operatorship of PEL 82 with a 55% participating interest, while QatarEnergy will hold 25%. Custos Energy retains its 10% interest in the licence, and Sintana maintains a 49% indirect interest in Custos.

As a result, Sintana's indirect exposure to PEL 82 remains unchanged following the transaction.
Through Custos, Sintana continues to participate in the exploration potential of the licence alongside its joint venture partners. The company said it looks forward to further evaluating and demonstrating the potential of PEL 82 as exploration activities progress.

PEL 82 is located offshore Namibia in the Walvis Basin and covers Blocks 2112B and 2212A. The licence spans approximately 11,450 square kilometres, with water depths ranging from 350 to 2,300 metres.
Existing seismic data covers approximately 70% of the licence area, providing a substantial technical dataset for exploration planning. Previous drilling on the licence includes the Wingat-1 and Murombe-1 wells.

The addition of QatarEnergy as a participating partner brings further international industry involvement to the offshore exploration licence, while Chevron remains responsible for operatorship.
